content:
The [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. A random inspirational quote from a curated list — change the seed for another. Enter your seed (change it for another quote) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Get a random inspirational quote from a curated list of 30 well-known quotations — Steve Jobs on loving your work, Henry Ford on believing in yourself, Confucius on persistence, and more. Every quote carries its standard attribution, and the list is fixed, so the same seed always gives the same quote. Change the seed (or use the generate button) for a different one. Quotes are shown for inspiration; they are short excerpts, used with attribution.

## How to use the Random Quote Generator

Start by entering your seed (change it for another quote). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Read the quote shown — the author is listed underneath.
2. Change the seed number (or press generate) for another quote.
3. The same seed always gives the same quote, so you can share a seed to share a quote.

## Formula

A uniformly distributed random index into a fixed list of 30 attributed quotes. Change the seed for another draw.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. With the seed set to 1 the generator shows: “Imagination is more important than knowledge.” — Albert Einstein. Change the seed to 2 and a different quote appears. Try the same figures in the [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Seed (change it for another quote): 1), the [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) returns Quote: “Imagination is more important than knowledge.”, Author: Albert Einstein, Quote number: 8 of 30. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Random Picker](/random-picker) is worth a look before you finish.

## About the quotes

The list is 30 short, well-known quotations with their standard attributions — the wording people actually quote. Famous sayings are often paraphrased or misattributed over time, so the list sticks to the versions that are widely documented. If you need a quote for publication, check the wording against a reliable source first.

## How the random pick works

The generator uses a deterministic seeded random number, the same approach as the other random tools on this site: the seed picks the quote, so the result is reproducible. Change the seed and the pick changes. Nothing is random in the cryptographic sense here — these are inspirational quotes, not passwords, so a seeded pick is the right tool.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Change the seed to browse the list — there are 30 quotes to find.
- Use the quote number to jump back to a favourite: the same seed always returns it.
- For a presentation, verify the wording against a reliable source before you publish it.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many quotes are in the list?

30 well-known quotations, each with its standard attribution — from Steve Jobs, Henry Ford, Confucius, Einstein, Mandela and others. Try it with your own numbers in the [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I get the same quote again?

Yes — the generator is seeded, so the same seed always gives the same quote. Note the seed (or the quote number) and come back to it any time. Try it with your own numbers in the [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Are the quotes correctly attributed?

Each quote carries its standard, widely documented attribution. Famous sayings are sometimes paraphrased, so check a reliable source before publishing one. Try it with your own numbers in the [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Random Quote Generator use?

A uniformly distributed random index into a fixed list of 30 attributed quotes. Change the seed for another draw. You can see it in action in the [Random Quote Generator](/random-quote-generator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
